- [ ] Investigate this statement: "The existing mutation lock under .git is also questionable and should eventually move behind a proper lock abstraction."
- [ ] Fix .git isolation in orka project:
  - Agents can currently do whatever to the shared git state since all of project .git is mounted rw.
  - Possibly introduce MCP or other specific tooling to let the agent do git actions without actual access to the raw .git dir.
- [ ] Should be able to specify some part of some file for a change.
  The node created for that work should be associated with the node which created that output.
- [ ] View a typed turn answer in the Styra interface.
  The server side exists: a turn sent with a `contract` is framed and recorded,
  and `turn_answer` returns the parsed `AnswerValue` for a live or stored
  session (`styra-server/src/contract.rs`, `protocol/README.md`). Nothing in
  the interface asks for one or renders it, so a typed answer is currently only
  reachable from a client like `examples/typed_answer.rs`.
  - Ask for a shape: a way to attach a contract to the composer's message,
    and some indication in the timeline that the turn was typed — the operator
    should be able to see the instructions their message was actually sent
    with (`contract::instructions`) rather than wondering what was appended.
  - Render the answer per contract rather than as the prose it arrived in:
    `files` as a navigable list (it already carries path, line, column and
    description — the same fields a jump needs), `lines` as a list, `json`
    pretty-printed, `text` as it is.
  - Re-read an existing answer under another contract, which the protocol
    already supports via `turn_answer`'s optional `contract` field. Cheap to
    expose and it makes a mis-shaped answer recoverable without asking again.
  - Decide what happens when the parse fails, which is the common case worth
    designing for: the `Answer` carries the `source` message it was parsed
    from, so the interface can show the reply verbatim and say why it did not
    satisfy the contract, rather than reporting an error with nothing in it.
